name: Easy Order – Simple Store Builder
author: MD RUBEL MIA

sections.description:
Easy Order (also searched for as COD Order Manager or a Cash on Delivery plugin for WordPress) lets you sell directly from any page or post with a single shortcode – no shopping cart, no checkout redirect, and no WooCommerce installation or payment gateway account required to get started. A customer clicks Buy Now, fills in their details right there on the page, and the order is placed with Cash on Delivery (COD) or Offline payment (bank transfer / pay later). Every order lands in your own Orders screen, ready to filter, search, and update with a click.

It’s built for local businesses, service providers, single-product stores, dropshippers, and anyone who wants a fast “buy this one thing” flow without the overhead of a full shop plugin – while still scaling up cleanly if you later add WooCommerce, or need online payment gateways like PayPal, Stripe, Razorpay, and SSLCommerz, SMS/WhatsApp order alerts, OTP fraud protection, or automatic discounts (all available in the separate COD Order Manager Pro add-on).

Why store owners choose it

  • No WooCommerce required – runs completely standalone on any WordPress site, out of the box.
  • One-click Buy Now checkout – no cart, no multi-step checkout, no forced account creation.
  • Cash on Delivery and Offline payment work immediately – no API keys, no gateway sign-up, no waiting for approval.
  • Your own product catalog – categories, tags, stock tracking, a Sale badge, and a bulk CSV importer.
  • A homepage-ready Hero Slider for promoting products, offers, or announcements.
  • A full marketing landing page for any single product – hero photo, price, Buy Now, feature highlights, and “Related Products”/”Newest Arrivals” sections, in a modern “Dark Premium” design (or a Light alternative), fully colorable from Settings.
  • An “Order via WhatsApp” button next to Buy Now, pre-filled with the product, price, and link – a free wa.me click-to-chat link, no API key or paid provider needed.
  • Coexists cleanly with WooCommerce if you already have it – the two checkouts never collide, and you can even merge both catalogs into one grid.

Shortcodes and what each one is for

[comw_product id="123"] – Sell a single item from Easy Order’s own built-in product catalog. Shows the thumbnail/gallery, title, price, and an inline Buy Now button with the checkout panel already wired up. Use this for a dedicated product page or a promoted item embedded in a blog post.

[comw_buy_button id="123"] – The universal buy button. Point it at any priced post – Easy Order’s own catalog, a WooCommerce product (simple, variable, or external/affiliate), or any other post type you’ve registered via a filter – and it resolves the price, image, and stock fresh from the database every time. Also works with no product behind it at all:

[comw_buy_button title="One-Hour Consultation" price="49.99"]

for a one-off service or item that doesn’t need its own product page. Perfect for a pricing table, a landing page call-to-action, or a “Buy Now” link dropped into an existing WooCommerce product page.

[comw_product_list] – A full catalog grid (or list) with a grid/list toggle, a left-hand sidebar of filters that only render when they’re actually useful (price range, category, tags, attributes, rating, and stock status), and a click-to-preview image popup with an auto-rotating gallery. New pages load either with a “Load More” button or automatically via infinite scroll as the visitor reaches the bottom – your choice, set once in Settings. Attributes:

  • title – an optional heading shown on the same line as the “Showing X of Y products” count and grid/list toggle (default: none)
  • post_type – comw_product (default, your own catalog), product (list WooCommerce products instead), or both_product (merge your own catalog and WooCommerce’s into one combined grid)
  • per_page, columns, view (grid or list)
  • group_by_category – yes to show a “Shop by Category” layout instead: a heading and its own small grid (starting with per_page products) for every category that actually has published products, one after another. Each category gets its own independent “Load More” button (loading more of just that category, not the whole page) once it has more than per_page products, plus a “View All” link to its own archive. No filter sidebar or infinite scroll in this mode – each category grid is its own self-contained query.
  • filters, filter_price, filter_category, filter_tags, filter_attributes, filter_rating, filter_stock – each can be set to no to hide that specific filter, or filters="no" to hide the whole sidebar (ignored when group_by_category="yes")

Use this for a shop-style archive page built entirely from a shortcode, without needing a full storefront theme or WooCommerce’s shop template.

[comw_hero_slider] – An auto-rotating image slider/banner for your homepage, landing page, or storefront header. Each slide has its own background image, heading (choose the HTML tag, H1-H6, for SEO control), subtitle, call-to-action button, text alignment/color, and color overlay. Manage slides with drag-to-reorder and global settings (autoplay, interval, dots, arrows, fade/slide transition, height, boxed/full width) under Easy Order > Hero Slider.

[comw_product_landing id="123"] – A full marketing-style landing page for one product: hero photo (or auto-sliding gallery), title, price, and Buy Now, an optional feature-chip strip pulled from the product’s own Specifications, and optional “Related Products” (same category) / “Newest Arrivals” sections. Two hero layouts (full-width image with the title over it, or a classic side-by-side split) and a “Dark Premium” or “Light” color scheme are set globally under Easy Order > Product Landing Page, along with colors, fonts, image sizing, and auto-slide timing – any of it can be overridden per shortcode instance, e.g. show_related="no". Give a product its own Landing Page Images (Product Manager) for a hero photo distinct from its catalog thumbnail, or leave it empty to fall back to the Featured Image + Product Gallery automatically.

[comw_category_showcase] – A “Search by Category” row for your homepage or landing page: a horizontally-scrolling set of category cards (image + name), each linking straight to that category’s own archive. Give a category its image under Easy Order > Products > Categories (Add/Edit Category screen) – a category with none set falls back to a plain placeholder icon rather than an empty box. Attributes:

  • title – the heading text (default “Search by Category”); leave empty (title="") to hide the heading entirely
  • taxonomy – comw_product_cat (default, this plugin’s own catalog), product_cat (WooCommerce’s categories instead – only when WooCommerce is active, otherwise falls back to this plugin’s own), or both (merge both catalogs’ categories into one row – each keeps using whichever “category image” field its own admin screen already offers: this plugin’s Add/Edit Category screen for its own categories, WooCommerce’s own Thumbnail field for WooCommerce’s)
  • count – how many categories to show (default: all)
  • parent – 0 (default) shows only top-level categories; pass a category ID to show its subcategories instead
  • orderby, order – name (default), count, term_id, or menu_order; ASC (default) or DESC
  • hide_empty – yes to hide categories with no published products (default: no, so a category still shows even before its first product is added)
  • show_arrows – no to hide the prev/next scroll buttons

[comw_order_lookup] – A self-service “Track My Order” form. A customer enters their Order ID and the email they ordered with and sees the order’s current status, item, and total – no account or login required. Wrong ID or wrong email both return the same generic message, so the form can’t be used to probe whether a given order ID or email exists. Drop this on its own “Track Your Order” page and link to it from your order confirmation email or footer menu.

[comw_order_confirmation] – The order confirmation/thank-you page content, auto-created for you on activation (find it under Easy Order > Settings) – you don’t normally need to place this manually.

Your own product catalog

  • A full product editor under Easy Order > Products – title, description, short description, regular/sale price, a unit label (e.g. “1kg”), featured image, and an image gallery, with an “All Products” list screen (search, status tabs, category filter, sortable columns, bulk trash/restore/delete) and stat tiles for total units sold and total stock remaining.
  • Categories and tags for your catalog, managed from their own submenu screens – shown automatically as filters on [comw_product_list] and assignable right from the product editor, including adding a new category inline without leaving the page. Give a category its own image for a [comw_category_showcase] “Search by Category” row.
  • CSV product importer – upload a WooCommerce product export (or any CSV using the same column names) to bulk-create or bulk-update products. Large files are processed in batches so it works regardless of catalog size or host time limits; only columns Easy Order has a home for are imported, and unsupported rows (variable/grouped/external products) are skipped with a reported reason instead of silently dropped. Re-uploading a corrected file updates products already imported under the same title instead of duplicating them.
  • Stock tracking – track an exact quantity (auto-reduced when an order completes, shows “Out of Stock” at zero) or just flip a manual In Stock / Out of Stock switch. Checkout re-verifies stock server-side every time, never trusting what the page happened to show. Existing products with no stock setting at all stay purchasable.
  • Fixed Quantity packages – sell something that only makes sense as a set number of units (a 20kg sack, a box of 6, a bundle of 3) by setting a Fixed Quantity on the product. The quantity field is locked at checkout so a customer can’t accidentally order “20” sacks instead of one 20kg sack – Regular Price is simply the price of the whole package.
  • A fully customizable “Sale” badge (position, colors, border radius, size, spacing) and a struck-through original price, shown automatically wherever a price is discounted.

Checkout Fields

Preview exactly what your checkout panel asks customers for – Full Name, Email, Phone, Delivery Address, City, Postal Code, and Country – under Easy Order > Checkout Fields. Reordering fields, changing labels/validation, hiding fields you don’t need, and adding your own custom fields (text, email, phone, textarea, dropdown, checkbox, or radio) is unlocked by COD Order Manager Pro.

Every product page sells itself

A product’s own permalink page is purchasable the moment you publish it – Easy Order automatically adds the Buy Now box (image, price, description) to the page even if you never pasted a shortcode into it. It also prints a matching <meta name="description">/og:description tag from the product’s short description for search engines and social previews, automatically stepping aside if Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, or The SEO Framework is already active.

Everything else it does

  • Cash on Delivery and Offline payment, ready the moment you activate – just a label to customize, no API keys or sandbox accounts.
  • Variable and external/affiliate WooCommerce products, fully supported: attribute dropdowns resolve the real variation and its price live, and an external product renders as a clean “View Product” link instead of a checkout form.
  • A “Buy Now” button on WooCommerce’s own single product pages too (classic and block themes both), right alongside – or in place of, once a gateway is configured – the normal Add to Cart.
  • Optional shipping fee (flat, or a different rate per city) and a single tax rate, applied automatically to every order based on what the customer enters in the City field.
  • An “Order via WhatsApp” button, shown next to Buy Now wherever it appears (catalog cards, product pages, the landing page) once you add your WhatsApp number under Settings – opens a chat pre-filled with the product, price, and link, no API key required.
  • An Orders screen with AJAX status filtering, search, CSV export, and one-click status changes – no page reloads.
  • Add New Order – record a sale that came in outside the storefront (WhatsApp, phone call, Facebook, etc.) straight from the Orders screen, tagged with its own Order Source, exactly as if the customer had checked out themselves.
  • Automatic Steadfast Courier consignment creation – once an order is marked Completed, a consignment is created on Steadfast automatically (API Key/Secret Key under Easy Order > Settings > Courier), tracking code and status shown right on the order.
  • Customizable Buy Now / Pay Now button text, under Easy Order > Settings > Product Display.
  • Automatic email notifications to both the customer and the site admin when an order is placed and again when it’s marked completed.
  • Runs standalone, or opt in to run alongside WooCommerce – Easy Order defers to WooCommerce by default so the two checkouts never collide, falling back to WooCommerce’s own Add to Cart automatically anywhere it isn’t configured to take over.

Built with security in mind

  • Every AJAX request is nonce-protected and price/stock/variation data is always re-verified fresh on the server – nothing from the browser is ever trusted for what a customer actually gets charged.
  • Order confirmation, payment-return, and cancellation links use a signed, unforgeable per-order token, so an order ID alone (a plain sequential number) can never be used to view someone else’s order.
  • The guest order-lookup form never reveals whether a wrong Order ID or a wrong email address was the mismatch, and is rate-limited per visitor.
  • CSV exports are formula-injection safe.
  • All admin actions check the current user’s capability before making any change.

Need more? COD Order Manager Pro adds:

  • 4 more payment gateways – PayPal, Stripe, Razorpay, and SSLCommerz, configured in the same Settings screen.
  • Discount Rules – automatic discounts by product, category, price, day of the week, date, or coupon code, with usage limits and rule stacking.
  • A full Checkout Fields editor – edit every built-in field and add unlimited custom fields.
  • Sales Reports – revenue, top products, top customers, payment-method breakdowns, and period-over-period comparison.
  • SMS & WhatsApp order notifications – connect any SMS/WhatsApp provider’s API, no vendor lock-in.
  • OTP phone verification at checkout – block fake/fraudulent Cash on Delivery orders with a one-time SMS code, required only for the payment methods you choose.
  • Ad pixel tracking – Facebook Pixel, TikTok Pixel, and Google Ads/GA4 conversion tracking, wired to real order data.

Support

For support, please use the plugin’s support forum on WordPress.org.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the sjrubel-cod-order-manager folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install it directly from the Plugins screen in your WordPress admin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the “Plugins” screen in WordPress.
  3. Go to Easy Order > Settings to enable Cash on Delivery and/or Offline payment, and set general options (currency, shipping, tax, pagination style, Sale badge appearance).
  4. Add a product under Easy Order > Products (or import a batch via the Import Products button), then paste its [comw_product id="X"] shortcode on any page – or use [comw_product_list] to show your whole catalog at once.
  5. Optional: add a few slides under Easy Order > Hero Slider and place [comw_hero_slider] on your homepage.
sections.faq:
Do I need a payment gateway account to use this?

No. Easy Order ships with Cash on Delivery and Offline payment, both of which need nothing but a label – no API keys, no gateway account.

Do I need WooCommerce to use this?

No. Easy Order works entirely on its own. If WooCommerce is also active on your site, it stays off by default so the two checkouts never collide – you can opt in to running it alongside WooCommerce from Easy Order > Settings.

Can I sell a WooCommerce product without WooCommerce’s cart/checkout?

Yes, once enabled alongside WooCommerce. Use [comw_buy_button id="123"] with a WooCommerce product ID, and a “Buy Now” button also appears on that product’s own page – for simple and variable products. If Easy Order isn’t set up to take over yet, that button automatically falls back to WooCommerce’s own normal Add to Cart instead. External/affiliate products always link straight to the seller’s own site, since WooCommerce itself never processes their payment either.

Can customers check their order status without an account?

Yes – add the [comw_order_lookup] shortcode to any page. They enter their Order ID and the email they ordered with, no login required.

Can I organize my products into categories, or bulk-import them?

Yes to both. Categories and tags are managed under Easy Order > Products > Categories/Tags (or right from the product editor, including adding a new category on the fly), and the Import Products button on the Products screen accepts a CSV file – a WooCommerce product export works, or any CSV using the same column names.

Can I track stock for my own products?

Yes – each product under Easy Order > Products has an Inventory box where you can either track an exact quantity or manually mark it In Stock / Out of Stock. Existing products with no stock setting at all stay purchasable, so nothing you already have live suddenly disappears from sale.

What is “Fixed Quantity” for?

It’s for products that only make sense as one fixed-size package – a 20kg sack, a box of 6, a bundle of 3. Set a Fixed Quantity on the product and the quantity field at checkout is locked to that exact number, so customers can never accidentally multiply the price by ordering “20” of something that should only ever be ordered as one package. Just make sure Regular Price is the price of the whole package, not a single unit.

Can I show a “browse by category” row with images on my homepage?

Yes – add [comw_category_showcase] to any page for a horizontally-scrolling row of category cards (image + name), each linking to that category’s own archive. Set each category’s image from Easy Order > Products > Categories, on that category’s own Add/Edit screen.

Can I add a slider or banner to my homepage?

Yes – the [comw_hero_slider] shortcode shows a fully customizable, auto-rotating image slider. Add and reorder slides (background image, heading, subtitle, button, text color, overlay) and control autoplay/timing/transition under Easy Order > Hero Slider.

Can I create a dedicated landing page for a single product?

Yes – add [comw_product_landing id="123"] to any page for a full marketing-style page for that one product: hero photo, price, Buy Now, a feature-highlight strip, and Related Products/Newest Arrivals sections. Colors, hero layout, image sizing, fonts, and auto-slide timing are all set under Easy Order > Product Landing Page, and any of the show/hide sections can be overridden per shortcode instance.

Can customers order or ask about a product over WhatsApp?

Yes – add your WhatsApp number under Easy Order > Settings > General Settings and an “Order via WhatsApp” button appears next to Buy Now everywhere it’s shown. Clicking it opens the customer’s own WhatsApp with a message already filled in (product, price, link) addressed to your number – they still have to press Send themselves, so it’s a free, no-API contact channel rather than a guaranteed order. Requires nothing but a phone number – no WhatsApp Business API, no paid provider.

Can I edit the checkout fields or add my own custom field?

The free plugin shows you a preview of the checkout fields (Full Name, Email, Phone, Delivery Address, City, Postal Code, Country) under Easy Order > Checkout Fields. Editing labels/validation/order, hiding fields, and adding unlimited custom fields (text, email, phone, dropdown, checkbox, radio) requires COD Order Manager Pro.

How do the [comw_product_list] filters work?

Each filter (price, category, tags, attributes, rating, stock) only appears when it’s actually applicable – your own product catalog has categories, tags, and stock status but no WooCommerce-style attributes or ratings, while a WooCommerce catalog shows attributes and ratings instead of tags. You can also disable any individual filter, or the whole sidebar, via shortcode attributes.

Where do orders go?

Orders are stored separately from WooCommerce orders, in their own Orders screen under the Easy Order admin menu.

Can I record a sale that came in over WhatsApp, a phone call, or Facebook?

Yes – click + Add New Order on the Order Lists screen, pick the product and quantity, fill in the customer’s details, and choose an Order Source (WhatsApp, Phone Call, Facebook, Instagram, or Other). It’s saved as a real order – same pricing math, emails, and stock reduction as if the customer had checked out themselves – with its source shown on the order and in the CSV export.

Can I automatically create a courier consignment when an order is completed?

Yes, for Steadfast Courier – enter your API Key and Secret Key under Easy Order > Settings > Courier and turn it on. The moment an order is marked Completed (automatically by a payment gateway, or manually from the Orders screen), a consignment is created on Steadfast and its tracking code/status is shown on that order. Off by default, and has no effect at all until you enable it – other couriers aren’t supported yet.

Can I change the “Buy Now” or “Pay Now” button text?

Yes – under Easy Order > Settings > Product Display, set “Buy Now Button Text” (shown on catalog cards, the product page, and the landing page) and/or “Pay Now Button Text” (the checkout popup’s submit button). Leave either empty to keep the default English text.

Can I add PayPal, Stripe, Razorpay, SSLCommerz, automatic discounts, SMS/WhatsApp alerts, or OTP fraud protection?

Yes, via the separate COD Order Manager Pro add-on, which plugs payment gateways, Discount Rules, a full Checkout Fields editor, Sales Reports, SMS/WhatsApp notifications, OTP checkout verification, and ad pixel tracking directly into this plugin’s existing Settings, Orders, and storefront screens – no separate configuration to learn.
sections.changelog:
1.0.5

  • New: Add New Order – record a sale placed outside the storefront checkout (WhatsApp, phone call, Facebook, etc.) directly from the Orders screen: pick a product/quantity, enter the customer’s details, and choose an Order Source. Creates a real order with the same pricing math, emails, and stock reduction as a normal checkout, and shows its source on the order detail view and in the CSV export.
  • New: Steadfast Courier integration – once enabled with an API Key/Secret Key (Easy Order > Settings > Courier), a consignment is created automatically on Steadfast the moment an order is marked Completed. The resulting tracking code/status (or an error, if the call failed) is shown on that order. Off by default and has zero effect until configured.
  • New: customizable “Buy Now” and “Pay Now” button text (Easy Order > Settings > Product Display) – shown on catalog cards, the product page, the landing page, and the checkout popup; leave either empty to keep the default text.

1.0.4

  • New: per-city shipping zones – charge a different flat shipping fee for each city (e.g. Dhaka 60, Rajshahi 100, Chittagong 120), matched against what the customer types in the City field at checkout, with a Default Shipping Fee for any city not listed. Set these up under Easy Order > Settings > Shipping. Also renamed “Flat Shipping Fee” to “Default Shipping Fee” – existing sites keep their currently configured value as the new default/fallback.
  • Changed: the Settings screen now has dedicated Shipping and Tax tabs (moved out of General), and Product List Pagination moved from General to the Product Display tab. Just reorganized – no setting’s saved value changes.
  • Improved: when shipping zones are set up, the checkout’s City field now shows autocomplete suggestions matching your configured city names, so a typo doesn’t silently fall back to the Default fee.

1.0.3

  • New: [comw_category_showcase] taxonomy attribute – show WooCommerce’s own product categories (taxonomy="product_cat") or merge them with this plugin’s own catalog categories (taxonomy="both") instead of only this plugin’s own catalog. Requires WooCommerce active; falls back to this plugin’s own categories otherwise.
  • New: [comw_product_list] title and group_by_category attributes – an optional heading inline with the product count/toggle, and a “Shop by Category” layout (a heading + small grid per category, each with its own independent “Load More” button and a “View All” link where there are more products than shown).
  • Fixed: the [comw_product_list] filter popup (toggle/drawer display mode) wasn’t usable on mobile – the dimmed background behind it now stays scoped to the product grid itself instead of covering the whole screen (including unrelated content above it), the panel opens in its original position instead of jumping to the top of the screen, and its close button no longer gets visually clipped.
  • Changed: Orders screen – “Delete Permanently” now works on an order of any status, not only once it’s already Cancelled; the submenu itself was renamed from “Orders” to “Order Lists”.
  • Improved: every Easy Order admin submenu item now shows a small icon next to its label for quicker visual scanning.

1.0.2

  • New: [comw_category_showcase] – a “Search by Category” row of category cards (image + name) for your homepage or landing page, with prev/next scrolling and a link to each category’s own archive.
  • New: an Image field on the Add/Edit Category screen (Easy Order > Products > Categories), plus a thumbnail column on the categories list – the image [comw_category_showcase] shows for that category.
  • New: “Order via WhatsApp” button next to Buy Now (catalog cards, product pages, the landing page) – a free wa.me click-to-chat link pre-filled with the product, price, and URL. Set your WhatsApp number, button text, and message template under Easy Order > Settings > General Settings; the button only appears once a number is set, and never shows for an out-of-stock item.

1.0.1

  • New: [comw_product_landing id="123"] – a full marketing-style landing page for one product: hero image/gallery, title, price, Buy Now, category badges, a feature-chip strip, and “Related Products”/”Newest Arrivals” sections, each independently toggleable per shortcode instance.
  • New: two hero layouts (full-width image with the title over it, or side-by-side) and a “Dark Premium” color scheme (amber accent, dark gradient hero/feature strip) as the new default, with a “Light” alternative – both fully colorable, and the hero image’s size/blur/opacity adjustable, from Settings.
  • New: dedicated Landing Page Images field per product (Easy Order > Products), shown exclusively on that product’s landing-page hero when set, or merged with its Featured Image + Product Gallery via a Settings toggle; falls back to the Featured Image + Product Gallery automatically when left empty.
  • New: hero image auto-slide, with separate on/off + interval controls for a product’s own Landing Page Images versus its Featured Image/Gallery fallback.
  • New: Buy Now on the landing page (and anywhere via [comw_product id="123" modal="yes"]) now pops the checkout into the same popup style used elsewhere on the site, instead of expanding inline.
  • New: redesigned Product Landing Page and Hero Slider admin screens – tabbed layout, toggle switches, drag-to-set range sliders, and card-style choice pickers, replacing the earlier long scrolling forms.
  • Fixed: a single-image landing-page hero (no gallery) wasn’t stretching to fill its container – now sizes correctly at any hero width.
  • Fixed: the Landing Page Images field’s remove button was invisible/unclickable due to missing styling.
  • New: Hero Slider – [comw_hero_slider] shortcode plus a drag-to-reorder admin screen for an auto-rotating homepage/landing-page image banner.
  • New: Fixed Quantity – lock the checkout quantity field for products that only make sense as one fixed-size package.
  • New: Checkout Fields preview screen under Easy Order > Checkout Fields (full editing and custom fields available via the Pro add-on).
  • New: both_product option for [comw_product_list] to merge your own catalog and WooCommerce’s into one combined grid.
  • Fixed: Fixed Quantity products were being priced as quantity x price instead of as a single package price – now always priced correctly as one package.
  • Improved: live checkout price preview now matches the corrected Fixed Quantity pricing.
  • New: [comw_product_list] sidebar filters – price range, category, tags, attributes, rating, and stock status, each conditionally shown based on what’s actually available.
  • New: infinite-scroll option for [comw_product_list], alongside the original Load More button – switch between them in Settings.
  • New: [comw_order_lookup] shortcode for self-service guest order tracking, rate-limited and enumeration-safe.
  • New: CSV product importer, categories/tags, and stock tracking for the plugin’s own product catalog, enforced on the storefront and re-verified server-side at checkout.
  • New: full support for WooCommerce variable products (live attribute/variation resolution) and external/affiliate products (clean link-out, no checkout attempted).
  • New: customizable “Sale” badge (position, colors, border radius, padding, size, margin) and a struck-through original-price display, shown automatically wherever a price is discounted.
  • New: tabbed Settings screen (Payment Gateways / General Settings), switching instantly with no page reload.
  • Improved: modernized storefront checkout panel and product-list card/grid design.
  • Fixed: WooCommerce products sold through this plugin’s own checkout now have their stock correctly checked and reduced, the same as products sold through WooCommerce itself.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.

short_description: Sell single products with a Buy Now button and Cash on Delivery or Offline payment - no cart, no checkout redirect, no WooCommerce required.

Shortcodes and what each one is for

[comw_product id="123"] – Sell a single item from Easy Order’s own built-in product catalog. Shows the thumbnail/gallery, title, price, and an inline Buy Now button with the checkout panel already wired up. Use this for a dedicated product page or a promoted item embedded in a blog post.

[comw_buy_button id="123"] – The universal buy button. Point it at any priced post – Easy Order’s own catalog, a WooCommerce product (simple, variable, or external/affiliate), or any other post type you’ve registered via a filter – and it resolves the price, image, and stock fresh from the database every time. Also works with no product behind it at all:

[comw_buy_button title="One-Hour Consultation" price="49.99"]

for a one-off service or item that doesn’t need its own product page. Perfect for a pricing table, a landing page call-to-action, or a “Buy Now” link dropped into an existing WooCommerce product page.

[comw_product_list] – A full catalog grid (or list) with a grid/list toggle, a left-hand sidebar of filters that only render when they’re actually useful (price range, category, tags, attributes, rating, and stock status), and a click-to-preview image popup with an auto-rotating gallery. New pages load either with a “Load More” button or automatically via infinite scroll as the visitor reaches the bottom – your choice, set once in Settings. Attributes:

  • title – an optional heading shown on the same line as the “Showing X of Y products” count and grid/list toggle (default: none)
  • post_type – comw_product (default, your own catalog), product (list WooCommerce products instead), or both_product (merge your own catalog and WooCommerce’s into one combined grid)
  • per_page, columns, view (grid or list)
  • group_by_category – yes to show a “Shop by Category” layout instead: a heading and its own small grid (starting with per_page products) for every category that actually has published products, one after another. Each category gets its own independent “Load More” button (loading more of just that category, not the whole page) once it has more than per_page products, plus a “View All” link to its own archive. No filter sidebar or infinite scroll in this mode – each category grid is its own self-contained query.
  • filters, filter_price, filter_category, filter_tags, filter_attributes, filter_rating, filter_stock – each can be set to no to hide that specific filter, or filters="no" to hide the whole sidebar (ignored when group_by_category="yes")

Use this for a shop-style archive page built entirely from a shortcode, without needing a full storefront theme or WooCommerce’s shop template.

[comw_hero_slider] – An auto-rotating image slider/banner for your homepage, landing page, or storefront header. Each slide has its own background image, heading (choose the HTML tag, H1-H6, for SEO control), subtitle, call-to-action button, text alignment/color, and color overlay. Manage slides with drag-to-reorder and global settings (autoplay, interval, dots, arrows, fade/slide transition, height, boxed/full width) under Easy Order > Hero Slider.

[comw_product_landing id="123"] – A full marketing-style landing page for one product: hero photo (or auto-sliding gallery), title, price, and Buy Now, an optional feature-chip strip pulled from the product’s own Specifications, and optional “Related Products” (same category) / “Newest Arrivals” sections. Two hero layouts (full-width image with the title over it, or a classic side-by-side split) and a “Dark Premium” or “Light” color scheme are set globally under Easy Order > Product Landing Page, along with colors, fonts, image sizing, and auto-slide timing – any of it can be overridden per shortcode instance, e.g. show_related="no". Give a product its own Landing Page Images (Product Manager) for a hero photo distinct from its catalog thumbnail, or leave it empty to fall back to the Featured Image + Product Gallery automatically.

[comw_category_showcase] – A “Search by Category” row for your homepage or landing page: a horizontally-scrolling set of category cards (image + name), each linking straight to that category’s own archive. Give a category its image under Easy Order > Products > Categories (Add/Edit Category screen) – a category with none set falls back to a plain placeholder icon rather than an empty box. Attributes:

  • title – the heading text (default “Search by Category”); leave empty (title="") to hide the heading entirely
  • taxonomy – comw_product_cat (default, this plugin’s own catalog), product_cat (WooCommerce’s categories instead – only when WooCommerce is active, otherwise falls back to this plugin’s own), or both (merge both catalogs’ categories into one row – each keeps using whichever “category image” field its own admin screen already offers: this plugin’s Add/Edit Category screen for its own categories, WooCommerce’s own Thumbnail field for WooCommerce’s)
  • count – how many categories to show (default: all)
  • parent – 0 (default) shows only top-level categories; pass a category ID to show its subcategories instead
  • orderby, order – name (default), count, term_id, or menu_order; ASC (default) or DESC
  • hide_empty – yes to hide categories with no published products (default: no, so a category still shows even before its first product is added)
  • show_arrows – no to hide the prev/next scroll buttons

[comw_order_lookup] – A self-service “Track My Order” form. A customer enters their Order ID and the email they ordered with and sees the order’s current status, item, and total – no account or login required. Wrong ID or wrong email both return the same generic message, so the form can’t be used to probe whether a given order ID or email exists. Drop this on its own “Track Your Order” page and link to it from your order confirmation email or footer menu.

[comw_order_confirmation] – The order confirmation/thank-you page content, auto-created for you on activation (find it under Easy Order > Settings) – you don’t normally need to place this manually.

Your own product catalog

  • A full product editor under Easy Order > Products – title, description, short description, regular/sale price, a unit label (e.g. “1kg”), featured image, and an image gallery, with an “All Products” list screen (search, status tabs, category filter, sortable columns, bulk trash/restore/delete) and stat tiles for total units sold and total stock remaining.
  • Categories and tags for your catalog, managed from their own submenu screens – shown automatically as filters on [comw_product_list] and assignable right from the product editor, including adding a new category inline without leaving the page. Give a category its own image for a [comw_category_showcase] “Search by Category” row.
  • CSV product importer – upload a WooCommerce product export (or any CSV using the same column names) to bulk-create or bulk-update products. Large files are processed in batches so it works regardless of catalog size or host time limits; only columns Easy Order has a home for are imported, and unsupported rows (variable/grouped/external products) are skipped with a reported reason instead of silently dropped. Re-uploading a corrected file updates products already imported under the same title instead of duplicating them.
  • Stock tracking – track an exact quantity (auto-reduced when an order completes, shows “Out of Stock” at zero) or just flip a manual In Stock / Out of Stock switch. Checkout re-verifies stock server-side every time, never trusting what the page happened to show. Existing products with no stock setting at all stay purchasable.
  • Fixed Quantity packages – sell something that only makes sense as a set number of units (a 20kg sack, a box of 6, a bundle of 3) by setting a Fixed Quantity on the product. The quantity field is locked at checkout so a customer can’t accidentally order “20” sacks instead of one 20kg sack – Regular Price is simply the price of the whole package.
  • A fully customizable “Sale” badge (position, colors, border radius, size, spacing) and a struck-through original price, shown automatically wherever a price is discounted.

Checkout Fields

Preview exactly what your checkout panel asks customers for – Full Name, Email, Phone, Delivery Address, City, Postal Code, and Country – under Easy Order > Checkout Fields. Reordering fields, changing labels/validation, hiding fields you don’t need, and adding your own custom fields (text, email, phone, textarea, dropdown, checkbox, or radio) is unlocked by COD Order Manager Pro.

Every product page sells itself

A product’s own permalink page is purchasable the moment you publish it – Easy Order automatically adds the Buy Now box (image, price, description) to the page even if you never pasted a shortcode into it. It also prints a matching <meta name="description">/og:description tag from the product’s short description for search engines and social previews, automatically stepping aside if Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress, or The SEO Framework is already active.

Everything else it does

  • Cash on Delivery and Offline payment, ready the moment you activate – just a label to customize, no API keys or sandbox accounts.
  • Variable and external/affiliate WooCommerce products, fully supported: attribute dropdowns resolve the real variation and its price live, and an external product renders as a clean “View Product” link instead of a checkout form.
  • A “Buy Now” button on WooCommerce’s own single product pages too (classic and block themes both), right alongside – or in place of, once a gateway is configured – the normal Add to Cart.
  • Optional shipping fee (flat, or a different rate per city) and a single tax rate, applied automatically to every order based on what the customer enters in the City field.
  • An “Order via WhatsApp” button, shown next to Buy Now wherever it appears (catalog cards, product pages, the landing page) once you add your WhatsApp number under Settings – opens a chat pre-filled with the product, price, and link, no API key required.
  • An Orders screen with AJAX status filtering, search, CSV export, and one-click status changes – no page reloads.
  • Add New Order – record a sale that came in outside the storefront (WhatsApp, phone call, Facebook, etc.) straight from the Orders screen, tagged with its own Order Source, exactly as if the customer had checked out themselves.
  • Automatic Steadfast Courier consignment creation – once an order is marked Completed, a consignment is created on Steadfast automatically (API Key/Secret Key under Easy Order > Settings > Courier), tracking code and status shown right on the order.
  • Customizable Buy Now / Pay Now button text, under Easy Order > Settings > Product Display.
  • Automatic email notifications to both the customer and the site admin when an order is placed and again when it’s marked completed.
  • Runs standalone, or opt in to run alongside WooCommerce – Easy Order defers to WooCommerce by default so the two checkouts never collide, falling back to WooCommerce’s own Add to Cart automatically anywhere it isn’t configured to take over.

Built with security in mind

  • Every AJAX request is nonce-protected and price/stock/variation data is always re-verified fresh on the server – nothing from the browser is ever trusted for what a customer actually gets charged.
  • Order confirmation, payment-return, and cancellation links use a signed, unforgeable per-order token, so an order ID alone (a plain sequential number) can never be used to view someone else’s order.
  • The guest order-lookup form never reveals whether a wrong Order ID or a wrong email address was the mismatch, and is rate-limited per visitor.
  • CSV exports are formula-injection safe.
  • All admin actions check the current user’s capability before making any change.

Need more? COD Order Manager Pro adds:

  • 4 more payment gateways – PayPal, Stripe, Razorpay, and SSLCommerz, configured in the same Settings screen.
  • Discount Rules – automatic discounts by product, category, price, day of the week, date, or coupon code, with usage limits and rule stacking.
  • A full Checkout Fields editor – edit every built-in field and add unlimited custom fields.
  • Sales Reports – revenue, top products, top customers, payment-method breakdowns, and period-over-period comparison.
  • SMS & WhatsApp order notifications – connect any SMS/WhatsApp provider’s API, no vendor lock-in.
  • OTP phone verification at checkout – block fake/fraudulent Cash on Delivery orders with a one-time SMS code, required only for the payment methods you choose.
  • Ad pixel tracking – Facebook Pixel, TikTok Pixel, and Google Ads/GA4 conversion tracking, wired to real order data.

Support

For support, please use the plugin’s support forum on WordPress.org.
